WHAT TO BUILD:
A. libreoffice.py
   - A `SvgConverter` typing.Protocol with a method `convert(self, source: Path, output_dir: Path) -> Path` returning the produced .svg path. This is the injectable port so tests never need the real binary.
   - `LibreOfficeSvgConverter` implementing it by running the real binary:
     `<soffice> --headless --norestore --convert-to svg --outdir <output_dir> <source>`
     Verified working command on this machine: C:\Program Files\LibreOffice\program\soffice.exe (takes ~10-20s per deck). Use subprocess with an explicit timeout, no shell=True, and raise a typed error (subclass RuntimeError with a machine-readable `code` attribute, following the StructuralExtractionError pattern in adapters/base.py) on non-zero exit, timeout, or missing output.
     - `discover_soffice()` returning `Path | None`: check the SOFFICE_PATH env var, then PATH (`shutil.which("soffice")`), then the two standard Windows install locations under Program Files and Program Files (x86). Used later by a doctor report, so keep it pure and side-effect free.
     - A `converter_version(soffice: Path) -> str` helper running `--version` and parsing the version string (e.g. "LibreOffice 25.2.5.2"); on any failure return "unknown".
B. SVG splitting: LibreOffice emits ONE .svg containing every slide. Verified structure (I confirmed this by probing real output):
   - root <svg> with many nested <g>; each slide is `<g class="Slide" id="...">` containing `<g class="Page">`.
   - Non-drawing pages carry only Background/BackgroundObjects/DateTime/Footer/PageNumber/Header children; real slides have at least one other child.
   - Provide `split_slides(svg_text: str) -> tuple[str, ...]` returning one standalone SVG document per real slide: keep the root <svg> attributes (width/height/viewBox/xmlns/xmlns:xlink), keep <defs> if present, and put exactly one Slide <g> inside. Preserve element ids exactly as LibreOffice emitted them (downstream code resolves shapes by those ids — never renumber, never strip them).
C. assets.py — asset externalization. LibreOffice inlines every drop-shadow and picture as a base64 `data:` URI inside `xlink:href`/`href` on <image> elements, which bloats a 5-shape slide to ~500KB. Provide:
   `externalize_assets(svg_text: str, assets_dir_name: str = "assets") -> tuple[str, tuple[RenderAsset, ...]]`
   - find every data URI (`data:<media-type>;base64,<payload>`), decode it, hash it with sha256, name the file `asset_<sha256>.<ext>` (ext from the media type: image/png -> png, image/jpeg -> jpg, image/svg+xml -> svg), deduplicate identical payloads by hash, rewrite the attribute to the relative path `<assets_dir_name>/asset_<sha>.<ext>`, and return the rewritten SVG plus one RenderAsset per unique asset (relative_path/media_type/content_sha256/byte_size).
   - The returned SVG must contain zero occurrences of the substring "data:image". Reject (typed error) any data URI whose media type is not in an allowlist of image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/svg+xml — never write an arbitrary attacker-chosen extension to disk.
   - Provide `write_assets(assets: tuple[RenderAsset, ...], payloads: Mapping[str, bytes], output_dir: Path) -> None` writing each asset under output_dir with parents created, refusing to escape output_dir. Design the return of externalize_assets so the caller can get the raw bytes (return a third element or a small frozen dataclass holding path->bytes; your choice, but keep it typed and documented).
D. Font extraction: PPTX may embed fonts under ppt/fonts/*.fntdata. LibreOffice does NOT emit @font-face at all (verified: zero @font-face in real output), so this layer only reports what exists. Provide `extract_fonts(pptx_path: Path, output_dir: Path) -> tuple[EmbeddedFont, ...]`: read the zip, for each embedded font part write it under `fonts/<family>.fntdata` and return EmbeddedFont(family=..., relative_path=..., embedded=True); for font families referenced by the deck theme but not embedded, return EmbeddedFont(family=..., embedded=False). Keep it bounded (reject absurd part counts/sizes) and never execute or parse font internals.

TDD IS MANDATORY AND CHECKED: for every behavior, write the failing test FIRST, run it, confirm it fails for the right reason, then implement. Tests must not require LibreOffice: use a fake SvgConverter plus small inline SVG fixtures you build in the test (or python-pptx-built decks like tests/conftest.py does).
